Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 25. Non-Governmental Organizations and/or Community Organizations and/or Community Groups are community groups formed participatively and become government partners in women's empowerment and child protection. 26. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, transfer, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 27. Minimum Service Standards hereinafter referred to as SPM is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing services for handling reports/complaints, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence. 28. Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for the Regional Government in carrying out activities for the implementation of empowerment and protection of women and children. 29. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 30. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 31. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 32. Complaint is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families or the community. 33. Health services are efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects. 34. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction to be able to carry out social functions properly. 35. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 36. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is Gender sensitive. 37. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 38. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 39. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.

Article 5

1. The Regional Government formulates policies, programs, and Gender Responsive development activities which are set forth in:
a. Regional Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMD);
b. Strategic Plan of SKPD; and
c. Work Plan of SKPD.
2. The formulation of policies, programs, and Gender Responsive development activities as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through Gender Analysis.

Article 27

1. P2TP2A has the principal task of carrying out part of the Regional Government's duties in providing services quickly, appropriately and in an integrated manner in efforts to Empower Women and Protect Children from acts of violence, discrimination and trafficking in persons.
2. In carrying out the duties as referred to in paragraph (1), P2TP2A has the following functions:
a. implementing facilitation and provision of protection services for women and children from discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, which are of an emergency nature quickly covering various services namely information, medical referral, legal, psychological, psychic, safe house (shelter), home visit and skills training as well as other forms of services that support the implementation of P2TP2A activities;
b. implementing coordination and building a synergistic network with Regional Apparatus, related Agencies, and/or other institutions that have duties and functions in the field of Women's Empowerment and Protection of Women and Children; and
c. monitoring of victims after handling by P2TP2A and/or work partners.

Part Two

Purpose and Objectives

Paragraph 1

P2TP2A

Article 26

1. In order to provide protection services for women and children from acts of violence, the Regional Government shall establish P2TP2A as an integrated service center in implementing programs and activities for the protection of women and children.
2. The establishment, Organization, and Work Procedures of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Regent Regulation.
